To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the brain is a dynamic system that develops through the interaction of the individual and his or her environment, (2) the brain is the product of the individual's interaction with the world, and (3) the brain is not a passive receptor of information, but an active participant in the construction of knowledge about the world.
1) The development of multimodal perception and action is an emergent process, 2) the process is dynamic and 3) the process is top–down.
the top–down processing of the human brain is the result of a long process of learning and experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of the body and its senses in the development of knowledge, and the role of this knowledge in the development of the individual’s sense of self, their world and the relationships between these two.
the development and use of knowledge in our everyday interactions with the world.
understanding how the mind develops, and the role that perception and action plays in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are playing in the streams of knowledge, and this play is a key component in our development of our world and our selves.

dynamic systems theory is a means for understanding how our world is created through the interplay between our sensory modalities and our world, and that this interplay allows us our autonomy and freedom in the world.

the dynamic systems approach to perception and action is a means to understand our development of knowledge about our world and ourselves, and that this development is a process that is top–down in its nature, and thus that our play and participation in the world are important for our autonomy and our aesthetic experiences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human mind is a dynamic system, and it is the dynamic system of the mind that allows us to develop and maintain knowledge about the world.

our perceptions are not just about the world but also for the world, and thus we can be seen to be playing in the world, as we are playing with our knowledge about it, which is constantly changing and developing.
the dynamic systems theory of perception is an important tool for understanding how we come to know our world and ourselves through the development of knowledge in our perceptual modalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can see how our perceptions and actions are not just a product of the world, but also a product of us as individuals, as well as a product of our participation in a world that is meaningful to us.
the world is not a passive object that we interact with, but a world that we participate in.
we are not just passive recipients of sensory information but rather active participants in a meaningful world, where the world we perceive is the world that we enact.
